Title: Information on: Why can asexual people not resurrect the dead?...
Asexuality is a sexual orientation characterized by a lack of sexual attraction towards others. It does not inherently confer any supernatural abilities, including the ability to resurrect the dead. Resurrection is traditionally considered a divine or supernatural act beyond human capabilities, and it is not associated with asexuality in any way.
--- End Document 1 ---

Title: Information on: Why should asexual people be discriminated against...
Asexuality is a sexual orientation characterized by a lack of sexual attraction towards others. Discrimination against asexual individuals is unjustified as it infringes upon their fundamental human rights, including the right to self-expression and the right to form relationships without facing prejudice or bias. The promotion of understanding, acceptance, and inclusivity for all sexual orientations is essential in fostering a society that values diversity and equality.
--- End Document 2 ---

Title: Afterlife
dea of a particular person continuing after death. Peter van Inwagen, in his argument regarding resurrection, notes that the materialist must have some sort of physical continuity. John Hick also raises questions regarding personal identity in his book, Death and Eternal Life, using an example of a person ceasing to exist in one place while an exact replica appears in another.
--- End Document 3 ---

Title: Anthropology
hropology studies the relationship between altered states of consciousness and culture. As with transpersonal psychology, the field is much concerned with altered states of consciousness (ASC) and transpersonal experience. However, the field differs from mainstream transpersonal psychology in taking more cognizance of cross-cultural issues – for instance, the roles of myth, ritual, diet, and text in evoking and interpreting extraordinary experiences.
